cases.question: What is the minimum notice required for a pre-arrival notice?
cases.source_text: Port of Kochi - Rules for Visiting Vessels (2026, fictional training document) 1. Arrival notice Ship agents must send the pre-arrival notice to the Harbour Master at least 72 hours before the vessel's expected arrival. Vessels carrying dangerous goods must send the dangerous goods declaration at least 48 hours before arrival. 2. Pilotage Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels longer than 50 metres. Pilot requests must be made at least 6 hours before the required boarding time. Night pilotage between 22:00 and 05:00 is available only for vessels with a draught below 10 metres. 3. Berthing Berths are allocated by the Port Operations Centre on a first-come, first-served basis, except for passenger ships, which have priority at the Cruise Terminal. A berth not used within 2 hours of the allocated time may be given to another vessel.

cases.source_text: # Port of Kochi - Crew Shore Leave (fictional training document) ## Shore passes Crew members may go ashore with a shore pass issued by the immigration office at the port gate. The ship agent must submit the crew list to immigration at least 24 hours before arrival. Shore passes are valid only within the city limits of Kochi. ## Hours Shore leave is allowed between 06:00 and 23:00. Crew must be back on board before 23:00; late return must be reported to the Harbour Master by the master of the vessel. ## Restrictions Crew of vessels in quarantine, or of vessels without a valid crew list, are not allowed ashore. Crew may not carry more than 2 litres of alcohol or 200 cigarettes when returning on board. ## Seafarers' centre The Kochi Seafarers' Centre near Gate 2 is open daily from 09:00 to 21:00 and offers free Wi-Fi, a small shop and transport to the city centre every hour.
